title: AI Writing Detectors: What to Do When Your Work Gets Flagged
content:
Bottom line: An AI-writing score is a reason to review a document, not proof that its author cheated. If you are a student, a freelancer or a manager, the useful next step is to preserve the writing process and check the applicable AI-use rules, not to keep trying detectors until one gives the answer you want.

Updated 8 October 2026. This is a documentation-based analysis, not a hands-on accuracy benchmark or legal advice. Examples below are hypothetical. No detector was tested for this article.

What an AI score actually tells you

First distinguish an AI-writing indicator from a plagiarism or similarity report. One estimates patterns associated with generated text; the other identifies overlap with material in a database. Neither, on its own, establishes why the overlap or pattern occurred.

Turnitin's report guidance says its AI indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. Its percentage concerns qualifying prose, not necessarily every word in a submitted file. A high score does not tell you what assistance the institution permitted.

The statistical trap: false positives are not a personal verdict

Turnitin's FAQ reports a document-level false-positive rate below 1% at the above-20% reporting threshold. That measures how often fully human documents are incorrectly flagged under its evaluation conditions. It does not mean a flagged document has less than a 1% chance of being human-written.

Here is a deliberately simplified example, not a Turnitin test. Suppose 1,000 documents contain 900 human documents and 100 AI documents. An imaginary detector flags 1% of human documents and catches 80% of AI documents. It flags 9 human and 80 AI documents: 9 of 89 flags, about 10%, are wrong. The error rate among human documents and the error rate among flagged documents answer different questions. Changing the share of AI documents changes the second answer.

Turnitin also published an approximately 4% sentence-level false-positive figure in June 2023. Treat that as a dated vendor claim, not a universal probability for any highlighted sentence today. Its model release notes document subsequent updates. Document-level and sentence-level numbers are not interchangeable.

If your essay or client draft gets flagged

  1. Keep the original file. Save the submitted version, date, assignment or brief, and the report if you can access it. Do not overwrite the disputed document.
  2. Collect genuine process evidence. Export available version history, outlines, notes and source links. Keep existing AI conversations if permitted and relevant. These are supporting context, not automatic proof. Do not fabricate drafts after the event.
  3. Read the rule that applied when you wrote it. Check the course handbook, client agreement or employer policy. Grammar assistance, brainstorming and AI-generated paragraphs may be treated differently.
  4. Ask for a specific review. Request the flagged passages, the tool and report date, and the rule allegedly breached. Ask how a human review or appeal works.
  5. Explain the process honestly. Describe how you developed the argument and checked references. If you used AI, explain what it did. A clean detector result would not excuse undisclosed use that violated an agreed rule.

Do not upload confidential client material or an unpublished assignment to a collection of free detector sites just to compare scores. Check the service's retention and privacy terms and whether you have permission to share the text.

A neutral review request

Please share the passages that triggered the AI-writing concern and the policy applied to my submission. I can provide my existing notes and available document history, and explain my research and drafting process. Could you confirm the human-review and appeal procedure before a decision is made?

Adapt that wording to your situation. It deliberately avoids claiming that version history conclusively proves authorship.

For teachers and managers: use a review checklist

  • Separate the automated indicator from the final decision.
  • Compare the concern with the actual assignment or workplace rules.
  • Check whether the input meets the tool's requirements. Turnitin requires at least 300 words of qualifying prose and does not reliably assess every format, such as code or tables.
  • Give the author a chance to explain the work and sources.
  • Record the reasons for the decision rather than copying a detector percentage into a verdict.

In the US and UK, the relevant starting point is the particular school's, university's or employer's published procedure. Do not assume that all institutions use the same threshold, or that a detector score creates a legal conclusion. For an important disciplinary dispute, consult the appropriate student support service, union representative or qualified adviser.

Why asking ChatGPT is not an authorship check

OpenAI's educator guidance says its own research did not find detectors reliable enough and it does not comment on other vendors' utility. It also warns that ChatGPT can invent answers to questions such as whether it wrote a passage. A chatbot's confident reply is not an audit trail.

Watermarks solve a different, narrower problem

Google's SynthID Text documentation describes a watermark inserted during generation. Detection is still probabilistic, with watermarked, not-watermarked and uncertain outcomes. It is not a universal yes/no authorship test.

A positive result for supported content can help establish provenance. A missing watermark does not prove human authorship: the content may come from another system or have been changed. Google's SynthID overview identifies text from the Gemini app and web experience among its supported uses. Do not assume all models, APIs or public verification interfaces have identical coverage.

The useful replacement for a detector contest

Before the next assignment or client project, agree on allowed assistance and what must be disclosed. Keep lightweight process records while working. For example, a freelancer can retain the brief, an outline, source notes and the final fact-check checklist. A student can keep research notes and ordinary document history. This costs less effort than defending a piece of finished prose using competing opaque scores.

Editorial correction: This update removes an access-check screenshot, clarifies the dated false-positive figures, narrows the OpenAI claim and corrects the earlier suggestion that text watermarking provides a certain yes/no answer.
